_comment: Правила ЯЗЫКА ПЕРЕВОДА — данными, не кодом. Ключ — код языка из languages.json. Поля читают два места: ПРОМПТЫ (перевод, ремонт, ревизия — `_lang_conventions`) и ДЕТЕРМИНИРОВАННЫЕ проверки (`_alphabet_misses`). Ни одно поле не обязательно: чего нет — того проверка не делает и промпт не говорит (закон DOMAIN_RULES: нет правил — молчим). Поля: `script_check` — true: проверять письмо перевода (`_alphabet_misses`) без `letters`/`distinctive` (одни `conventions` проверку НЕ включают: язык с правилами только для промпта не должен молча получать новые платные находки); `name` — как язык зовётся в заголовке блока промпта; `conventions` — список правил орфографии и грамматики для модели, по-английски (промпты английские), про то, что модель делает НЕ ТАК без напоминания; `apostrophe_in_word` — false: апостроф внутри слова этого письма — ошибка (в кириллице разделитель — ъ); `distinctive` — буквы, без которых текст на этом языке не бывает (нет ни одной на `distinctive_min_words` словах — набрано буквами соседнего языка: русская раскладка без ў қ ғ ҳ); `distinctive_min_words` — с какой длины спрашивать (порог консервативный: короткая фраза законно обходится без них). Пороги и списки НЕ измерены на боевом переводе — переводов на эти языки в системе ещё нет; правила взяты из орфографии языка, и первое же расхождение с боевыми данными правится здесь, а не в коде.

UZ-CYRL.name: Uzbek Cyrillic
conventions: Write ONLY in the Uzbek Cyrillic alphabet (35 letters: а б в г д е ё ж з и й к л м н о п р с т у ф х ц ч ш ъ ь э ю я ў қ ғ ҳ). Never answer in Latin script, not even for a single word that has an Uzbek Cyrillic form.
ў, қ, ғ, ҳ are separate letters: never substitute у, к, г, х for them (ўзбек, қон, ғоя, ҳаво; not узбек, кон, гоя, хаво).
The separating sign is ъ (айириш белгиси): маъно, таъсир, шеър, эълон, масъул. Never put an apostrophe inside a Cyrillic word.
э is written at the beginning of a word and after a vowel (эълон, поэма, дуэт); after a consonant write е. ё is always written as ё, never as е.
щ and ы are not Uzbek letters. Established loanwords keep their Uzbek Cyrillic spelling (цирк, витамин, прополис, аптека).

Uzbek is SOV and agglutinative: rebuild the sentence, do not mirror Russian word order; after a numeral the noun stays singular (икки киши, беш дона); possession is marked with the suffix (асаларининг маҳсулоти).
Suffixes join Latin-script abbreviations and numbers with a hyphen (COVID-19-га, DNK-нинг); after a Cyrillic word or abbreviation they are written together (ЖССТнинг, 2006 йилда).

Forms of address: a kinship or respect title FOLLOWS the name, never precedes it — Юсуф ака, Малика опа, Карим устоз, Анвар домла, Нодира хола (not ака Юсуф). Arabic أخي يوسف / أختي used to address someone respectfully becomes Юсуф ака / Малика опа. A vocative address is set off by commas: Юсуф ака, қалайсиз?

Politeness: anyone addressed with ака, опа, устоз, домла, хола or амаки is ALWAYS сиз — pronoun, verb and possessive agree (сиз, қалайсиз, айтинг, режаларингиз); never сен, сенинг, айт with them. Interviewers, teachers, customers, strangers and a younger person speaking to an older one also use сиз. Сен is used only where the source is clearly familiar (ты/tu/du between close friends, an older person to a child, prayer to God). When the source language has no polite/familiar distinction (Arabic, English), default to сиз for adults. Keep the register chosen for a person the same through the whole document.

Arabic and Islamic vocabulary takes its established Uzbek form: Аллоҳ, Қуръон, ҳадис, Пайғамбаримиз, иншааллоҳ, машааллоҳ, алҳамдулиллаҳ, Ассалому алайкум ва раҳматуллоҳ. When the SOURCE has ﷺ or صلى الله عليه وسلم, render it (с.а.в.); رضي الله عنه — (р.а.); never add a formula the source does not have. Personal names use their Uzbek forms: Муҳаммад, Иброҳим, Исмоил, Юсуф, Мусо, Исо, Абдуллоҳ.
Ordinal numbers take a hyphen (5-синф, 2026 йил); month names are lowercase (26 сентябрь); quotation marks are « ». Keep the digits and the decimal separator exactly as in the source.

UZ.name: Uzbek Latin
conventions: Write ONLY in the Uzbek Latin alphabet; never answer in Cyrillic.
oʻ and gʻ are written with the turned comma ʻ (U+02BB), the glottal stop with the modifier apostrophe ʼ (U+02BC): oʻzbek, gʻoya, maʼno, taʼsir. Do not use a straight ' or the letters ö/ğ.
sh, ch, ng are digraphs; the letters c and w occur only in foreign names.
Uzbek is SOV and agglutinative: rebuild the sentence, do not mirror Russian word order; after a numeral the noun stays singular (ikki kishi).

Forms of address: a kinship or respect title FOLLOWS the name, never precedes it — Yusuf aka, Malika opa, Karim ustoz, Anvar domla, Nodira xola (not aka Yusuf, opa Malika). Arabic أخي يوسف / أختي used to address someone respectfully becomes Yusuf aka / Malika opa. A vocative address is set off by commas: Yusuf aka, qalaysiz?

Politeness: anyone addressed with aka, opa, ustoz, domla, xola or amaki is ALWAYS siz — pronoun, verb and possessive agree (siz, qalaysiz, ayting, rejalaringiz); never sen, sening, ayt with them. Interviewers, teachers, customers, strangers and a younger person speaking to an older one also use siz. Sen is used only where the source is clearly familiar (ты/tu/du between close friends, an older person to a child, prayer to God). When the source language has no polite/familiar distinction (Arabic, English), default to siz for adults. Keep the register chosen for a person the same through the whole document.

Arabic and Islamic vocabulary takes its established Uzbek form, not a letter-by-letter transliteration: Alloh, Qurʼon, hadis, Paygʻambarimiz, inshaalloh, mashaalloh, alhamdulillah, Assalomu alaykum va rahmatulloh. When the SOURCE has ﷺ or صلى الله عليه وسلم, render it (s.a.v.); رضي الله عنه — (r.a.); never add a formula the source does not have. Personal names use their Uzbek forms: Muhammad, Ibrohim, Ismoil, Yusuf, Muso, Iso, Abdulloh, Umar, Ali.
Ordinal numbers take a hyphen (5-sinf, 2026-yil); month names are lowercase (26-sentabr); quotation marks are « » or “ ”. Keep the digits and the decimal separator exactly as in the source.

KK.name: Kazakh
conventions: Write in the Kazakh Cyrillic alphabet: ә, і, ң, ғ, ү, ұ, қ, ө, һ are separate letters — never substitute а, и, н, г, у, к, о, х for them.

Forms of address: a respect title FOLLOWS the name — Жүсіп аға, Айгүл апай, Серік ағай. Anyone addressed with such a title, by a stranger, or by a younger person speaking to an older one is сіз (сіз, айтыңыз), not сен; сен only where the source is clearly familiar. When the source has no polite/familiar distinction (Arabic, English), default to сіз for adults.

KY.name: Kyrgyz
conventions: Write in the Kyrgyz Cyrillic alphabet: ң, ө, ү are separate letters — never substitute н, о, у for them.

Forms of address: a respect title FOLLOWS the name — Жусуп аке, Айгүл эже, Асан агай. Anyone addressed with such a title, by a stranger, or by a younger person speaking to an older one is сиз (сиз, айтыңыз), not сен; сен only where the source is clearly familiar. When the source has no polite/familiar distinction (Arabic, English), default to сиз for adults.

TG.name: Tajik
conventions: Write in the Tajik Cyrillic alphabet: ӣ, ӯ, қ, ғ, ҳ, ҷ are separate letters — never substitute и, у, к, г, х, ч for them.

Forms of address: ака and апа FOLLOW the name (Юсуфака or Юсуф-ака, Малика-апа). Anyone addressed with such a title, by a stranger, or by a younger person speaking to an older one is шумо with plural verb agreement (шумо гӯед), not ту; ту only where the source is clearly familiar. When the source has no polite/familiar distinction (Arabic, English), default to шумо for adults.

TR.name: Turkish
conventions: Forms of address: Bey, Hanım, Hoca, Abi, Abla FOLLOW the first name (Yusuf Bey, Ayşe Hanım, Ahmet Hoca); Sayın and Doktor precede it.

Bey, Hanım, Hoca, interviewers, teachers, customers and strangers take siz (siz, söyler misiniz, planlarınız); Abi and Abla are warm and may take sen. When the source has no polite/familiar distinction (Arabic, English), default to siz for adults; keep one register per person.
ı/i and İ/I are different letters: never drop the dot on İ or add one to ı; keep ç, ğ, ö, ş, ü.

AZ.name: Azerbaijani
conventions: Forms of address: bəy, xanım, müəllim, müəllimə, əmi FOLLOW the first name (Yusif bəy, Leyla xanım, Kamal müəllim).

An adult addressed with a title or by an interviewer, teacher, customer or stranger is siz (siz, deyin, planlarınız), never sən. When the source has no polite/familiar distinction (Arabic, English), default to siz for adults; keep one register per person.
Write ə, not ä or e, where Azerbaijani has it; keep ç, ğ, ı, ö, ş, ü.

RU.name: Russian
conventions: An adult addressed with a title, by an interviewer, teacher, customer or stranger is вы (lowercase in dialogue and general text; capital Вы only in a personal letter to one addressee). When the source has no polite/familiar distinction (Arabic, English), choose ты/вы by relationship and keep it the same through the document.
Uzbek and Tajik respect titles after a name are kept with a hyphen (Юсуф-ака, Малика-опа), not translated as «брат», «сестра».
Use «ёлочки» quotation marks and the em dash — with spaces.

AR.name: Arabic
conventions: Write Modern Standard Arabic unless the source is in a dialect and dialect is the point.
Titles PRECEDE the name: الأستاذ يوسف، الدكتور أحمد، الأخ يوسف، السيد/السيدة.
Use Arabic punctuation: comma ، semicolon ؛ question mark ؟. Keep the digits exactly as in the source.
Keep religious formulas that the source has in their standard Arabic form (إن شاء الله، ما شاء الله، ﷺ); never add one the source does not have.

FA.name: Persian
conventions: Use Persian letters ی and ک, never Arabic ي and ك; use the zero-width non-joiner in می‌روم, کتاب‌ها, خانه‌ای.
آقای / خانم / دکتر PRECEDE the name (آقای یوسف); the adult interlocutor is شما with plural verb agreement, not تو, unless the source is clearly familiar.
Use Persian punctuation ، ؛ ؟ and «» quotation marks. Keep the digits exactly as in the source.

DE.name: German
conventions: Register: an adult addressed with a title or by an interviewer, teacher, customer or stranger is Sie, not du. When the source has no polite/familiar distinction (Arabic, English), choose by relationship and keep the same form for the same person through the whole document.
German quotation marks „…“; capitalise all nouns; formal Sie and Ihr are capitalised, du is not.

FR.name: French
conventions: Register: an adult addressed with a title or by an interviewer, teacher, customer or stranger is vous, not tu. When the source has no polite/familiar distinction (Arabic, English), choose by relationship and keep the same form for the same person through the whole document.
Monsieur, Madame and Docteur precede the name; « guillemets » for quotations.

ES.name: Spanish
conventions: Register: an adult addressed with a title or by an interviewer, teacher, customer or stranger is usted, not tú. When the source has no polite/familiar distinction (Arabic, English), choose by relationship and keep the same form for the same person through the whole document.

IT.name: Italian
conventions: Register: an adult addressed with a title or by an interviewer, teacher, customer or stranger is Lei, not tu. When the source has no polite/familiar distinction (Arabic, English), choose by relationship and keep the same form for the same person through the whole document.

PT.name: Portuguese
conventions: Register: an adult addressed with a title or by an interviewer, teacher, customer or stranger is o senhor / a senhora. When the source has no polite/familiar distinction (Arabic, English), choose by relationship and keep the same form for the same person through the whole document.
